explanation: The Escape handler is on the form's KeyDown, but this form's Designer never sets KeyPreview = True nor a CancelButton (only EditPolKey, ExportReg and EditPol set KeyPreview; grep the designers), so a key press on a focused control never reaches the form handler and Escape does not close the dialog. The claim that Escape closes it as cancelled is not shown by the code; re-read the Designer lines, and either drop the rule or state it as dead code (handler exists, not reachable). Also this text is repeated verbatim across many forms: one rule per decision, not copies.

The minus-sign clause is not shown: HexParseEditText uses ULong.Parse with NumberStyles.HexNumber, which does not allow a sign, so '-...' raises FormatException and falls to the catch-all (value unchanged), never OverflowException; the Minimum branch (line 48) is unreachable in practice (and Minimum is 0 anyway). The above-range case has two routes: text over ULong range (OverflowException) and text over the DWord Maximum (ArgumentOutOfRangeException when Value is set); both yield Maximum. Restate accordingly.

Same decision as businessrule-80613162490595796566 (Close/Escape reports OK iff an Apply was done, Cancel otherwise): CloseButton is the form's Cancel button with DialogResult.Cancel, and Click/FormClosed both apply the same test. Merge the two into one rule; note OK button always reports OK even if earlier state.

Claims every option is stored, but a dropdown option with no choice selected (no presentation default, or a stored value matching no item, which line 214 leaves unselected) makes Apply/OK fail: line 264 casts SelectedItem Nothing to read .ID, raising an unhandled exception, so nothing is stored (policy already forgotten at 242 only in the in-memory source). Add this refusal/failure outcome, and that label-only elements store nothing.

says: The outcome when Apply/OK is pressed with Enabled selected and a dropdown element left unselected is missing: the code throws (null dereference at the dropdown ID read) after the policy was already forgotten, and no message is shown. Write a rule for the dropdown element's required choice (or its absence of validation), citing the apply and default-selection lines.
